Documentation → Automation & Change Control → Calendar

Change calendar

One month, week, agenda or year view of every planned change request, every scheduled automation and what already ran — with overlap warnings, and a form to plan a new change straight from a day.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereOperations → Calendar (Global, FortiWeb and FortiADC consoles) (URL /calendar/)

What is it?#

The Calendar draws, on one grid, everything the fleet is scheduled to receive: change requests with their maintenance windows, scheduled actions projected forward from their schedules, and the runs that already happened. From any day you can plan a change, which raises a draft change request.

What does it do?#

  • Four views: month, week, agenda (the next 30 days) and year (counts only — click a month or a day for the detail).
  • Four bands you can show or hide: Planned changes, Automations (fleet work), System Automations (housekeeping) and What already ran.
  • Flags Overlapping changes on the same appliance — two changes whose windows overlap and that touch the same box — and Windows that can never open (a window ending at or before its start).
  • Opens a day panel listing that day's events, each linking to the page that owns it.
  • Plans a change against specific appliances, a group (tag, department, zone, line) or every appliance of the ADOM that the change type supports.

Requirements#

  • At least one change request or scheduled action to draw.
  • The Calendar switched on in your profile (it is on by default).

Permissions#

The page and the planner require users.manage (Administrator), the same as Change Requests and System Automations. Without it the Calendar entry is hidden and the URL answers 403.

Changes are filtered to the current ADOM the same way as on the Change Requests list; automations are filtered by the ADOM they were created in, and What already ran shows only runs of the current ADOM's automations.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the What already ran band shows only runs of the current ADOM's automations; before, it listed runs from every ADOM.

Switched off. Each user can switch the Calendar off in their profile. It then disappears from their Fleet menu and the URL shows Switched off for your account with Switch the Calendar back on. "Nothing was stopped. Approved changes and scheduled automations keep running on their windows whether or not this grid draws them."

How to use#

Read the grid#

  1. Open Operations → Calendar. Times are shown in the console timezone (named in the page header).
  2. Choose the view (month, week, agenda, year) and move with the previous / next arrows or Today.
  3. Under Show, toggle the bands. At least one of Planned changes, Automations, System Automations is always on ("The calendar always draws at least one of these."). What already ran only paints the past of the automation bands that are on.
  4. Tick Remember for me to keep the band selection on your profile; Clear forgets it.
  5. Click a day to open its panel; Open this day in full or Link to this day gives a shareable URL (?d=YYYY-MM-DD).

What each band draws:

Band Draws
Planned changes Each change request on its window; a change with no window yet is marked no window yet; an inverted window is shown on its start date as invalid window
Automations / System Automations Future fires of enabled automations, computed from their schedule. Disabled ones are not drawn (a note names them). A schedule that fires very often is capped per range, with a note
What already ran Recorded runs of the current ADOM's automations in the range: at most 400, most recent first; a note gives the total and points to the run history

A hidden band is counted and explained ("N of M … drawn") because a hidden automation still fires.

Plan a change from a day#

  1. Select the day, then fill in Plan a change ("This raises a Change Request in draft. It runs only once it is approved and scheduled — planning something here never executes it."): - Title and Type of change (documentary types are marked documentary). - What it touches: Specific appliances (Ctrl/Cmd-click), A group (tag / department / zone / line) with its value, or Every appliance in this ADOM the type runs against. - Window start / Window end (pre-filled 22:00–23:59 on the chosen day, in the console timezone), Risk, Responsible, Why, Rollback, Notify (emails, comma separated).
  2. Press Add to the calendar.
  3. The flash reads "CR-… raised as a draft — approve and schedule it to make it run." and the change request opens.

A group or ADOM selector is resolved to a fixed list of appliances the moment you save; the change records both the selector and the resulting list in its reason ("Planned from the calendar. Target selector: …"). Only appliances of products the chosen type supports are included.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Title Name of the change Yes Upgrade fweb-01 to 7.6.9
Type of change Change-controlled action or documentary type Yes Reboot the appliance (DESTRUCTIVE)
What it touches Specific appliances / a group / every appliance of the ADOM Yes Group · Zone = dmz
Window start / end Console timezone Start needed later to schedule 2026-11-07 22:00
Risk low, medium, high No (medium) high
Responsible Change owner No jdoe
Why / Rollback Reason and rollback plan No —
Notify Recipients of the maintenance notice (Mark notified) and the outcome notice No ops@example.com

The planner creates the change with Manual approval and the default document language; change them afterwards with Edit on the change request.

Example#

🧪Example — Plan a DMZ reboot window

In week view, select Saturday. In Plan a change choose type Reboot the appliance (DESTRUCTIVE), What it touches = A group, Zone = dmz, window 22:00–23:00, risk High, and press Add to the calendar. The change CR-2026-0031 is created as a draft naming the two FortiWeb appliances in zone dmz. After approval and scheduling, its window and the bound one-shot automation appear on Saturday.

Result#

  • A draft change request (see Change requests).
  • An audit entry calendar.plan with the reference, action and selector.
  • Nothing is executed until the change is approved and scheduled.

Troubleshooting#

"No visible appliance matches . Nothing was created."#

Possible causes — the group value matches no appliance in this ADOM, or none of the matching appliances is a product the type supports.

Solution — pick another group value or type, or switch to the ADOM that owns the appliances.

"Pick at least one appliance." / "Pick a group value."#

Solution — complete What it touches.

" is not a change-controlled action."#

Possible causes — the type was hidden or removed under Administrator → Change Types after the page was loaded.

Solution — reload the page and pick a type from the list.

"Your Calendar is switched off — nothing was created. …"#

Solution — switch the Calendar back on in your profile, then plan again.

An automation I know exists is not on the grid#

Possible causes — it is disabled, its band is hidden, it belongs to another ADOM, or it is a one-shot whose time has passed.

Solution — check the notes above the grid and the Show bands; open Scheduled actions in the right ADOM.

Advanced#

Advanced How events are computed
  • Future automation fires are projected from the schedule (never drawn on past days); the past comes only from recorded runs.
  • All ranges are computed in the console timezone and converted to UTC for the queries.
  • Each event links to the page that owns it: Automations or System Automations for an automation (by its scope), the change request for a change, the run history for a run.
  • The day panels of up to 400 events are pre-rendered; beyond that a day still opens through its own link.
